l.i: cùm ibi unà minime viueremus, permulti suspicari possent, me vel falsum, vel quoquo
modo hallucinatum. Quia homines astuci dant
intercurribus. At postea cùm ex Anglia in Germaniam
cum sub eodem tecto, cum eadem vixeris mensa, eorundem suavissimorum colloquiorum, exercitationum
& studiorum participes quoridie fuerimus. E-go unus omnium opinor me posse, de tua synce-
quae mi-bi experto & ἀυτόπτῃ[?] fuerunt compertissima.
atque aperte quid nam de te sentiam pateficere,
sed etiam tuas aures, quae semper fuerunt a propriis
Deinde minus dicam quam ipsa res
exigat, & a[?]tum agam, cùm ipse bene docendo, recte vinen-do, & functionem sibi commissam integerrime obeun-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "astuci" (possibly "astuti"); the Greek word after "experto" is uncertain; "a[?]tum" in the last paragraph is unclear, and "ad tum" may be read differently. Line-end hyphens in "E-go", "mi-bi" and "vinen-do" are printed. "obeun-" is the last printed line and a broken word, given here as the catchword. Dropped and unclear letters are marked with [?].
